Sessions

Reading Groups RGs

Biweekly discussions of protocol literature. Each session takes one or two readings from the library and works through them together, usually with a guest.

Diagram Jams DJams

Collaborative diagramming sessions: drawing research processes together, and arguing about how to represent agents, objects and the knowledge moving between them.

Conference Crashing

Members turn up at symposia and conference sessions, alone or in groups, to bring protocol questions into other fields' rooms.

Most recently: Symposium 'The Life of Protocols in the Life Sciences', ISHPSSB 2025, Porto.

Forming

SIG: Standardization & Variability in Biosciences

A special interest group on standardization in the scientific practices, mostly the empirical and experimental ones: how standards hold together, and what varies underneath them anyway.

sig

Share your interest

SIG: Integral Protocol Theory

A special interest group working towards an empirically-based transdisciplinary philosophy of protocolization

sig

Share your interest

SIG: Ethnography of the “Boring”

Taking up Susan Leigh Star's provocation to study boring things, and working out the methods for it — somewhere between archival and documentary research and ethnomethodology.

sig methods

Share your interest

SIG: The Procedural Mind

Where the micro-sociology of practice meets cognitive science and psychology: what following a procedure does to, and asks of, a mind.

sig cognition

Share your interest

Protocol Studies Concept Cartography

Mapping the conceptual space of protocol studies: definitions, characterisations, examples and the routes between ideas. Modelled on Concept Cartography, which grew out of a reading group on epistemic diversity and whose cartographers include two Protocollege members.
